newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico blue chips at new record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico blue chips at new record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended mixed on Wednesday, although blue chips edged up to record territory in a very selective recovery.
"We saw gradual profit taking through the day, but also buying that absorbed it," said Roberto Galvan, an analyst at the Bursametrica consultancy.

The blue chip IPC index ended up 4.69 points, or 0.11 percent, at a record 4,281.52. The broad market balance, however, was negative. Out of 108 stocks traded, decliners outpaced gainers by 45 to 42, with volume smaller than many recent sessions at 95.96 million shares.
Galvan said the broad market trend was due to light profit-taking rather than a sell-off, as overall volume was lackluster.
"This shows a trend among investors to hold positions," he added.

"Stocks recovered on delayed buying by small investors, who always step into a rally after the big players have bought," another analyst said. "The unemployment data were good, but did not explain the recovery.
"Lower inflation has halted the slide in purchasing power, but we still await a recovery in real income to boost consumption," the analyst added.

The National Statistics Institute announced during morning dealing that open unemployment in Mexico fell to 3.9 percent in May from 4.29 percent in April. A Reuters survey of 13 financial houses had predicted an average rate of 4.12 percent.
Dealers said, however, that strong industrial output data released Tuesday helped the blue chip recovery. A breakdown showed manufacturing and construction drove the increase.
"Cemex was one of the few interesting stocks today, although Alfa and GCC also did well," a floor trader said.

Cement maker Cemex CPO shares gained 55 centavos (7 cents) to 32.25 pesos ($4.08), while its B shares were up 65 centavos (8 cents) to 35.50 pesos ($4.49), and its A shares rose 65 centavos (8 cents) to 32.35 pesos ($4.08). All three share series are included in the IPC.
Cement stock Grupo Cementos de Chihuahua (GCC) ended up 10 centavos (1 cent) at 8.70 pesos ($1.10). Conglomerate Alfa, meanwhile, gained 60 centavos (8 cents) to 51.60 pesos ($6.53).

Financial group Bancomer A shares were the most heavily traded gainer of the day, up 8 centavos (1 cent) to 2.18 pesos (28 cents). Dealers said the stock gained at the expense of its B shares, which fell 11 centavos (1.5 cents) to 3.82 pesos (48 cents) after recent sharp gains.
Bancomer's two share series, which are both included in the IPC, accounted for 23 percent of all shares traded.
Telecomms stock Telmex weighed heavily on the market, and ended down 18 centavos (2 cents) at 18.52 pesos ($2.34), while its American Depository Receipts ended down 37.5 cents at $46.75.
The Dow Jones industrial average slumped 42.07 points to 7,718.71.
